headline: US markets took a hammering last night — NASDAQ down 4.2% — dragging tech holdings lower, while PLS had a rough day on the ASX as lithium sentiment stays weak.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had its worst session today, dropping 3.75% to $5.91. The broader ASX mining sector was in the red as lithium and gold stocks both slid. Sentiment around lithium remains deeply divided — some investors see a recovery coming, others think prices stay low for longer. PLS is now down 12.3% on your total investment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 2.66% last night to $416.67, the biggest dollar move in your portfolio. Despite a strong Microsoft Build 2026 conference with major AI announcements, the broader NASDAQ selloff (down 4.2%) dragged the stock lower. The US tech sector had one of its worst nights in recent memory.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 1.74% today to $18.05, reflecting the broader weakness in AI and tech stocks flowing through from last night's brutal NASDAQ session. The ETF holds global AI-exposed companies, so when US tech sneezes, this one catches a cold. You're down 5.15% on your investment.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.04% last night to $214.39, caught in the wider NASDAQ selloff rather than any company-specific bad news. GTA 6 buzz continues — there was a quirky story overnight about the game's real-life boss being added as a playable character, which at least keeps the title in the headlines. You're down 7.5% overall on this one.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 0.95% last night to $365.76, a relatively modest drop compared to the broader NASDAQ carnage. No company-specific news drove the move — it was general tech sector weakness. You're still up 26.6% on this position, the star of your US holdings.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 0.94% today to $92.03. Emerging markets copped a double hit — a falling AUD (down 1.16%) would normally help, but broader risk-off sentiment and a weaker global growth picture weighed on this one. Small position, small dollar impact.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL eased 0.8% today to $8.70, tracking a fall in crude oil prices (WTI crude dropped 2.69% to $90.54 last night). Oil fell broadly as global growth concerns crept back in. Despite today's dip, you're still up 2.86% on your investment in FUEL.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.31% today to $521.82, a small positive in an otherwise rough session. This ASX-listed ETF tracks the entire US share market and can sometimes move differently to US futures because of currency and timing effects. You're up 1.19% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG crept up 0.12% today to $75.95 — essentially flat. Its diversified mix of assets (Aussie shares, international shares, bonds) acted as a cushion on a tough day. Small but steady — you're up 0.76% on this one.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped 3.75% today to $5.91 and is now down 12.3% on your cost base. Lithium sentiment is stuck in the mud — analysts are genuinely split on whether prices recover. No near-term catalyst is obvious, so if you're uncomfortable with the drawdown, it's worth reviewing your conviction. For now, hold unless your thesis has changed.

watch_today.title: NASDAQ down 4.2% last night — brace for US open tonight
watch_today.detail: Last night's NASDAQ Composite fell 4.18% to 25,709 and the S&P 500 dropped 2.64% to 7,383. That's a serious risk-off move. Your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) will be in focus when Wall Street reopens tonight around 11:30 PM AEST — there could be further volatility or a bounce. Worth keeping an eye on.

watch_today.title: MSFT — hold through the noise
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 2.66% last night to $416.67, but this looks like broad market weakness rather than anything company-specific. Microsoft Build 2026 produced strong AI announcements this week, which is a long-term positive. Short-term pain, but the story hasn't changed. Hold.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF dip, but long-term story intact
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 1.74% today to $18.05 as global AI stocks followed the NASDAQ lower. Separately, Motley Fool Australia published a positive piece on ASX AI ETFs this week. The dip could be a buying opportunity if you believe in the AI decade thesis, but given broad market uncertainty right now, no rush to add.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cuts on the horizon — good news for VDHG
watch_today.detail: CBA is now forecasting RBA interest rate cuts ahead. Lower rates generally push up share and property prices, which is a tailwind for a diversified growth ETF like VDHG. Keep an eye on Tuesday's RBA commentary — if they signal cuts are coming, VDHG and the broader ASX could get a boost.

watch_today.title: AUD falling — impacts your US stock values
watch_today.detail: The Australian dollar dropped 1.16% to 70.5 US cents. A weaker AUD actually increases the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO), which softens the blow from last night's USD price falls. Worth knowing as you read your portfolio numbers.

markets.summary: Last night was a rough one on Wall Street — the NASDAQ fell over 4% and the S&P 500 dropped 2.6% in one of the bigger single-session selloffs in recent months. Tech stocks bore the brunt. Closer to home, the ASX 200 closed down a more modest 0.7% today at 8,625, with energy and mining stocks the main drags. Crude oil fell 2.7% last night to $90.54 a barrel, and gold dropped 3.1% to $4,337. The Aussie dollar slid to 70.5 US cents, down 1.16%.

politics.summary: The RBA and interest rates dominated local news this week, with CBA forecasting cuts ahead while the RBA deputy defended past hikes. Albanese is digging in on tax reform, and the Treasurer is facing heat over government debt.

stories.title: CBA forecasts RBA interest rate cuts coming
stories.why_it_matters: Commonwealth Bank — Australia's biggest home lender — is now officially forecasting that the Reserve Bank will cut interest rates. That's significant because CBA has a huge economics team and their forecasts move markets. Rate cuts mean cheaper mortgages, higher property values, and generally a boost for shares. If you're on a variable rate mortgage or holding growth assets like VDHG, this is good news on the horizon.

stories.title: RBA deputy defends past rate hikes as criticism mounts
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's deputy governor pushed back on criticism that the central bank raised rates too aggressively, saying it's easy to judge in hindsight. This comes as housing stress from past rate hikes is still very real for many Australians, and the debate about whether the RBA got it right is heating up. The RBA is also flagging early signs of a housing market slowdown as those rate rises start to bite.

stories.title: Albanese digs in on tax reform, says it's good for 'democracy and social cohesion'
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese is standing firm on proposed tax reforms despite pushback, framing them as good for Australian society. While full details weren't available in the article, Labor's tax reform agenda has included changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax (CGT) — the tax discount you get when selling an investment at a profit. If you own investment property or are planning to sell assets, this reform debate is worth tracking closely.

stories.title: Treasurer defends $53 billion debt burden — 'Not a lot'
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is defending the federal government's $53 billion debt level, describing it as manageable in the context of Australia's economy. Opposition critics are pushing back, arguing the spending is fuelling inflation and keeping interest rates higher for longer. The RBA itself was questioned on whether government spending is making its job harder — a key tension in Australian economic policy right now.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a rare moment of unity — the CEOs of OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft are jointly asking the US Congress to pass laws on synthetic DNA screening, worried that AI is making it dangerously easy to create bioweapons. Meanwhile, Trump's new AI executive order could reshape how AI models are launched in the US.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic & Microsoft CEOs unite to demand synthetic DNA screening laws
stories.why_it_matters: In a rare show of unity, the bosses of OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Microsoft and others signed an open letter calling on the US Congress to make synthetic DNA screening mandatory. Their argument: AI tools can now teach people how to engineer biological weapons, and synthetic DNA that could be repurposed for that is freely available online. This is the AI industry pre-emptively asking for regulation in a specific, high-risk area — which is unusual and signals just how serious they think the biosecurity risk has become.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has signed a new executive order (a presidential directive) that could force AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to change the process for how they release new AI models to the public. The details are still emerging, but it appears to involve new national security review steps before major model launches. This could slow down the release of new AI products and create a more regulated environment in the US — relevant to your GOOG and MSFT holdings.

stories.title: Microsoft Build 2026: 7 Biggest AI Announcements
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft's annual developer conference, Build 2026, wrapped up this week with a string of major AI announcements. Full article details weren't available, but the conference typically previews new AI features being baked into Windows, Azure (Microsoft's cloud), and the Copilot AI assistant. These announcements are bullish for Microsoft's long-term AI positioning — relevant to your MSFT holding — though last night's price drop shows the market is focused on broader macro concerns right now.

stories.title: UN calls for AI regulation as environmental footprint grows
stories.why_it_matters: The United Nations is calling for stronger regulation of AI, pointing to its rapidly growing environmental footprint — the massive amounts of electricity and water data centres use to run AI models. The UN's concern is that everyday AI usage (think ChatGPT searches, image generation) is quietly adding up to a significant carbon cost that current regulations aren't addressing. This is becoming a recurring theme alongside AI's economic impact, and something investors in AI stocks and ETFs should be aware of as a long-term risk.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 is well underway — the Storm survived a thriller against the Knights, the Roosters thumped the Raiders, and the Dolphins are currently leading the Cowboys in the first half. The French Open is heating up with a surprise finalist, and there's a big AFL clash locked in for today.

stories.title: Storm survive 32-30 thriller vs Knights — star player sent to hospital
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm edged out the Newcastle Knights 32-30 in a 62-point thriller at AAMI Park on Friday night. Fox Sports described it as a 'hell of a fight' with the Storm surviving a massive scare. The drama was compounded by a star player being sent to hospital during the match — a worrying sign for Storm's depth heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Sea Eagles beat Rabbitohs 28-14 — win comes at a cost
stories.why_it_matters: Manly Sea Eagles defeated South Sydney Rabbitohs 28-14 on Thursday night at 4 Pines Park. The win was solid but Fox Sports reports it came at a cost, with a controversial no-call from the referee drawing attention. The referee's explanation for the decision has already sparked debate — details are still emerging but the officiating decision was described as 'shock.'

stories.title: Roosters hammer Raiders 26-0 — Blues hopeful shines
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters put on a statement performance, thumping the Canberra Raiders 26-0 at GIO Stadium on Friday night. Fox Sports reported a 'stunning Blues audition' from one of the Roosters' wingers, with DCE (Daly Cherry-Evans) and Walker both igniting. The comprehensive win will put State of Origin selectors on notice with representative football looming.

stories.title: Mirra Andreeva into French Open final after sweeping Kostyuk 6-1, 6-3
stories.why_it_matters: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva is through to her first Grand Slam final after demolishing Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk 6-1, 6-3 in the French Open semi-final on June 4 at Court Philippe-Chatrier in Paris. It's a stunning result — Andreeva is one of the youngest players on tour and this is a massive breakthrough. She'll now fight for the Roland Garros title, with Australian tennis fans watching on and wondering when an Aussie will next reach this stage.

stories.title: Broncos vs Titans tonight at Suncorp — Gold Coast team in action
stories.why_it_matters: Your Gold Coast Titans are in action tonight at Suncorp Stadium against the Brisbane Broncos, with kick-off at 7:35 PM. Big local rivalry game — keep an eye on it. The Dolphins are also playing right now against the Cowboys in Townsville (leading 16-10 at half-time), looking to extend what is reportedly a record winning streak.
